The solar system was born about 4.6 billion years ago from a massive cloud of gas and dust, known as the solar nebula, which collapsed under its own gravity. This collapse led to the formation of a rotating disk, with the Sun forming at its center as nuclear fusion ignited. The remaining material in the disk gradually coalesced into planetesimals, which grew into planets. The inner solar system, where it was too hot for volatile compounds to remain solid, formed rocky planets like Earth, while the outer regions gave rise to gas giants like Jupiter and Saturn. The early solar system was chaotic, with frequent collisions shaping planets, forming moons, and creating craters. Over time, the solar system stabilized, paving the way for the emergence of life on Earth.
